inputs.original_text: Five months after a ceasefire was announced in Gaza, airstrikes are still killing civilians, and the humanitarian situation remains dire There is little left that connects Palestinians in Gaza with their prewar existence. The contours of life have become darker and far more brutal, as if the population has been stripped from its past. “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen,” said 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: They announced a ceasefire five months ago, yet airstrikes are still killing civilians and daily life in Gaza remains under drones, gunfire, shelling, and fire directed at fishermen. That contradiction is the point: the ceasefire label gives powerful institutions a story of progress while the reality on the ground keeps getting more brutal. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says the drones “never stop buzzing overhead.” This looks less like peace and more like a managed narrative designed to make ongoing destruction easier to ignore.
